Title: User stays logged in for a full 30-minute session on mobile
Preconditions: Backend running; user jdoe exists with password password123
Steps: 1. Open the app on a mobile browser | 2. Log in with valid credentials | 3. Wait 2 minutes | 4. Send a chat message
Expected Result: The access token's expires_in is 1800 seconds (30 minutes); the chat request at the 2-minute mark succeeds without being prompted to log in again

Title: Full login -> chat -> silent refresh -> continued use flow
Preconditions: Backend and Streamlit UI both running
Steps: 1. Log in via /auth/login | 2. Call /chat successfully | 3. Wait until under 60s remain on the access token | 4. UI auto-calls /auth/refresh | 5. Call /chat again with the new access token
Test Data: username=smishra, password=password123, message="What is the insurance policy?"
Expected Result: The UI transparently refreshes the token before expiry and the second /chat call succeeds with agent=hr_agent
Priority: with no visible logout to the user

Title: Access token expires exactly at the SESSION_TIMEOUT_MINUTES boundary
Preconditions: SESSION_TIMEOUT_MINUTES=30 in .env; valid access token issued at time T
Steps: 1. Log in and record token exp claim | 2. Wait until system clock passes exp by 1 second | 3. Call GET /auth/me with the expired token
Expected Result: Request is rejected with 401 and detail 'Session expired or invalid. Please log in again.' -- NOT a 10-second expiry as in the original IMS-4 bug

Title: Refresh token successfully rotates and issues a new valid session
Preconditions: User has a valid, unexpired refresh_token from a prior login
Steps: 1. POST /auth/refresh with the valid refresh_token | 2. Inspect the response | 3. Call GET /auth/me with the new access_token
Expected Result: Response is 200 with a new access_token different from the old one and expires_in=1800; /auth/me returns the correct username

Title: Reusing an already-rotated (or revoked) refresh token is rejected
Preconditions: User has refreshed once already, so the original refresh_token is no longer active
Steps: 1. POST /auth/refresh with the original (already-used) refresh_token | 2. Observe the response
Test Data: the stale refresh_token from before rotation
Expected Result: Request fails with 401 'Refresh token revoked or unknown.' confirming old tokens cannot be replayed to extend a session indefinitely

Title: Chat endpoint rejects requests with no or invalid token
Preconditions: Backend running, no Authorization header or a malformed token
Steps: 1. POST /chat with message body but no Authorization header | 2. POST /chat with Authorization: Bearer garbage-token
Expected Result: Both requests return 401 Unauthorized and no agent response body is returned

Title: Login with invalid credentials is rejected
Steps: 1. POST /auth/login with username=jdoe and an incorrect password
Expected Result: Response is 401 'Incorrect username or password.' and no tokens are issued

Title: Chat message about leave policy routes to the HR agent
Steps: 1. Log in | 2. POST /chat with a leave-related question
Expected Result: Response agent field equals 'hr_agent' and response text is a non-empty string (fallback message if leave.pdf has no extractable text)

Title: HR agent gracefully handles an empty/placeholder PDF instead of crashing
Preconditions: data/leave.pdf and data/insurance.pdf are present but 0 bytes (placeholder files)
Steps: 1. Log in | 2. POST /chat asking about insurance
Expected Result: Response is 200 with a friendly fallback message stating the policy document is unavailable
Priority: instead of a 500 error or stack trace

Title: Logout revokes the refresh token so it cannot be used afterward
Preconditions: User has a valid refresh_token from an active session
Steps: 1. POST /auth/logout with the refresh_token | 2. POST /auth/refresh with the same refresh_token
Expected Result: Logout returns {""status"": ""logged_out""}; the subsequent refresh attempt fails with 401 since the token was revoked
